heroLead: Vandergrift was built as a planned steel town along the Kiskiminetas River, and the families who've stayed here for generations often hold onto mineral rights that go back to before the mill itself was finished.
intro: Vandergrift sits along the Kiskiminetas River in Westmoreland County, a borough originally planned around the Apollo Iron and Steel Company's works at the turn of the twentieth century. Land ownership around Vandergrift has stayed relatively stable across generations for a company town of its size, and mineral rights attached to older residential and farm tracts here often haven't changed hands since well before the Marcellus boom began.

The Kiski valley has seen Marcellus wet-gas leasing and development activity over the past decade and a half, and family tracts around Vandergrift have, in places, ended up inside modern drilling units.

sections.heading: Stable Ownership, But Rarely Reviewed
paragraphs: Because so many Vandergrift-area families have held the same property for generations, mineral interests here often haven't been looked at closely since a lease was first signed, sometimes over fifteen years ago. That's exactly the kind of situation where an outdated lease or an unreviewed royalty statement can be quietly costing a family money without anyone noticing.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We confirm your deed, check whether your parcel sits inside an active unit, review any lease and division order paperwork, and factor in post-production deductions honestly if a well nearby is already producing. From there we give you a clear, explained cash offer.

faqs.question: My family has owned this land since before the steel mill closed. Does that affect our mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but longstanding ownership often means the mineral rights were never formally reviewed or updated. We help confirm exactly what your current deed covers.

faqs.question: Is there active gas development near Vandergrift?
faqs.answer: The Kiski valley has seen leasing and unit activity over the years. We check current DEP records against your specific parcel to confirm what applies to you.

faqs.question: What if I've never received a royalty check at all?
faqs.answer: That could mean your interest is unleased, or it could mean a lease exists but no well has been drilled on your specific unit yet. We can help you determine which situation applies.

faqs.question: My deed lists the old Apollo Iron and Steel Company as a prior owner. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can, if the company reserved or sold mineral rights separately from the surface at some point. We trace that chain of title carefully so you know exactly what remains with your family today.
